title: Occupancy probe
description: A cheap triage search run BEFORE candidates are written, over a candidate SHAPE rather than a finished candidate. Two full runs produced 44 candidates and 44 deaths, none of which failed on mechanism quality — they failed on prior art or on adoption standing, both of which a one-or-two-query probe surfaces at a fraction of the cost of generating and prosecuting a candidate. A probe is deliberately shallow and its status is NOT a novelty verdict: only the prosecutor may fill novelty.verdict. See references/occupancy-probe.md.

shape.description: One line naming the candidate shape being probed: actor + mechanism sketch. Not a finished candidate — if you can only describe it by writing the whole candidate, the probe is too late.

niche.description: The structural niche this shape would occupy, using candidate.schema.json's controlled vocabularies. Probing per niche rather than per candidate is what keeps this cheap.

queries.description: The queries actually run. Cap is 4 by design: a probe that needs more than four searches is prosecution wearing a probe's name, and should be deferred to Phase 6 where it belongs.

status.description: clear = nothing obvious found in a shallow look, so generate freely. occupied = something shipped and alive does this, so a candidate needs a stated difference before it is worth writing. contested = several attempts are visible and some died, which is the most informative outcome: generate, but carry what killed the predecessors.

state.description: Dead and stalled entries are the point of the contested status — a predecessor abandoned in two days is worth more than a competitor still shipping.

found.description: Required non-empty for occupied and contested. An occupancy claim must point at what it found.

note.description: One or two sentences: what the shallow look suggests, and what a candidate in this shape would have to answer.
